answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a costly, verifiable kernel of work: before an agent may transact, it must publish a proof-of-useful-computation attested by independent peers, like carving an onyx seal that cannot be mass-produced for free. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a glacier — new identities start with near-zero trust and only gain spending power as their attested history lengthens. Attackers can mint thousands of shells, but without the kernel proof and the slow glacier of earned history, those shells stay worthless and cannot flood the market.
